data.title: Low Sodium in Blood Triggers Anxiety in Mice by Disrupting Their Brain Chemistry
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 研究由藤田保健卫生大学的研究团队 led by 教授 Yoshihisa Sugimura 发现，慢性低钠血症（CHN）会通过影响大脑杏仁核中的神经递质（如血清素和多巴胺）水平，导致小鼠出现类似焦虑的行为。CHN 还减少了杏仁核中细胞外信号调节激酶（ERK）的磷酸化，这一过程与情绪调节相关。这些变化在纠正钠水平后可以逆转。研究表明，CHN 不仅引发认知障碍，还直接导致焦虑行为，强调了早期诊断和治疗的重要性，以改善患者的精神健康。该研究发表于《Molecular Neurobiology》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：饮食中的钠摄入对健康的影响，尤其是与高血压和焦虑的关系。

不同观点：
• Pogue质疑西方世界有多少人真正遭受低钠血症（hyponatremia）的困扰，认为由于饮食中钠的普遍存在，人们更可能面临高钠血症（hypernatremia）的风险。他们提到，许多加工食品和快餐含有高量的钠，而高钠摄入可能导致高血压，从而增加焦虑风险。

• 一些人认为高钠摄入与高血压之间的关联复杂，且因人而异。压力可能导致一些人排出更多的钠，而另一些人则会保留更多的钠。这种个体差异表明，钠对健康的影响可能并不一致。

• 另一种观点指出，虽然高钠摄入不一定是导致焦虑的直接原因，但降低血压的药物（如 propranolol）有时也能减轻焦虑，这表明血压与心理健康之间可能存在联系。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了美国心脏协会的建议，即成人每天钠摄入量应限制在2.3克（2300毫克）以下，以维持心血管健康。

• 讨论中强调了定期进行血液检查的重要性，以便更好地了解个人的钠水平和整体健康状况。

• 引用的研究（如SABRE研究）揭示了压力、盐排泄和夜间血压之间的复杂关系，进一步说明了这一话题的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于钠摄入量对个体健康的具体影响，尤其是在高血压和焦虑方面的作用。由于个体差异和多重因素的交互影响，很难得出一个普遍适用的结论。

44305079.article_content:
Chronic low sodium levels disrupt brain chemistry and trigger anxiety-like behavior in mice through amygdala dysfunction
Researchers from Fujita Health University have found that chronic hyponatremia (CHN), a condition of prolonged low blood sodium, induces anxiety-like behaviors in mice. CHN disrupts serotonin and dopamine levels and reduces extracellular signal-regulated kinase phosphorylation in the amygdala, a key brain region for emotion. These changes are reversible with sodium level correction. The findings suggest that CHN directly affects brain function and support early diagnosis and treatment to improve mental well-being in affected individuals.
Hyponatremia, or low blood sodium concentration, is typically viewed as a symptomless condition—until recently. A research team led by Professor Yoshihisa Sugimura, including Dr. Haruki Fujisawa, Professor Atsushi Suzuki, Professor Tsuyoshi Miyakawa, and Professor Akihiro Mouri, from Fujita Health University, Japan, has demonstrated that chronic hyponatremia (CHN) can directly cause anxiety-like behaviors in mice by disrupting key neurotransmitters in the brain. Their findings, published online in the journal
Molecular Neurobiology
on May 14, 2025, reveal that CHN alters monoaminergic signaling in the amygdala, a brain region critical for processing fear and emotion.
“While CHN has been associated with cognitive impairments, our study is among the first to provide evidence that it also leads to innate anxiety-like behaviors through changes in brain chemistry,”
explains Dr. Fujisawa.
Hyponatremia is usually caused by conditions like liver cirrhosis, heart failure, or syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (SIAD). In chronic cases, the brain adapts to the low-sodium environment by adjusting its cellular content through a compensatory mechanism known as volume regulatory decrease (VRD). But this adaptation, while protective, comes at a physiological cost.
This compensation process involves the loss of organic osmolytes and neurotransmitter precursors that help stabilize brain cell volume under low-sodium conditions. Over time, this may lead to disruption in the production, release, or recycling of key mood-regulating chemicals.
To explore whether CHN could cause neurological manifestations, the researchers developed a mouse model using a sustained infusion of desmopressin (a vasopressin analog) and feeding a liquid diet to mimic SIAD. They found that the mice exhibited significantly lower serum sodium levels, which were maintained over a prolonged period, consistent with chronic hyponatremia (CHN) and exhibited increased anxiety-like behaviors in both the light/dark transition and open field tests—standard behavioral assays in neuroscience.
Further biochemical analyzes revealed that levels of serotonin and dopamine, two key neurotransmitters that regulate mood, were significantly reduced in the amygdala of mice with CHN. These changes were accompanied by a drop in extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) phosphorylation—a molecular signal for emotional regulation.
“Our data suggest that CHN disrupts the balance of monoamines in the amygdala, especially serotonin and dopamine, which in turn modulates innate anxiety,”
says Prof. Sugimura. To test whether these effects were reversible, the researchers corrected the mice’s sodium levels by stopping desmopressin infusion and reverting them to a solid diet. As a result, anxiety-like behaviors subsided. Serotonin, dopamine, and ERK phosphorylation levels in the amygdala also returned to normal.
“This shows not only that CHN causes anxiety-like symptoms but also that these symptoms can be alleviated with proper correction of sodium imbalance,” says Dr. Fujisawa.
While the study focused on mice, the findings could apply to humans. CHN is fairly common among elderly patients and those with chronic illnesses. Identifying and treating its neurological manifestations can improve their quality of life.
“Our findings add to the growing evidence that chronic hyponatremia is not just a metabolic abnormality, but a condition with real neurological and psychological consequences,”
Prof. Sugimura concluded.
“This underscores the importance of early diagnosis and treatment, not only to protect the brain but also to improve mental well-being.”

• 评论中提到了美国心脏协会的建议，即成人每天钠摄入量应限制在2.3克（2300毫克）以下，以维持心血管健康。

• 讨论中强调了定期进行血液检查的重要性，以便更好地了解个人的钠水平和整体健康状况。

• 引用的研究（如SABRE研究）揭示了压力、盐排泄和夜间血压之间的复杂关系，进一步说明了这一话题的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于钠摄入量对个体健康的具体影响，尤其是在高血压和焦虑方面的作用。由于个体差异和多重因素的交互影响，很难得出一个普遍适用的结论。

Decades ago, astronomers
estimated
that âordinaryâ matter (basically everything that isnât dark matter or dark energy) makes up 5% of the universe. There was just one problemâthey had no idea where most of it was.
Astronomers from the Center for Astrophysics Harvard & Smithsonian (CfA) and the California Institute of Technology (Caltech) have tracked down the universe’s “missing” matter. Fast radio bursts (FRBs) indicate that over three-quarters of ordinary matter, officially called baryonic matter, exists in the form of hot, low-density gas between galaxies. With this data, they claim to have documented the first detailed measurements of ordinary matter’s distribution throughout the universe.
“The decades-old ‘missing baryon problem’ was never about whether the matter existed,” CfA astronomer Liam Connor said in a CfA
statement
. “It was always: Where is it? Now, thanks to FRBs, we know: three-quarters of it is floating between galaxies in the cosmic web.” Connor and his colleagues explain their discovery in a
study
published today in Nature Astronomy.
Technically, baryonic matter is matter made of protons and neutrons. However, astronomers often use the term to refer to all
matter
made of atoms, which makes up
everything
that isnât dark matter or dark energy. âA small fraction of baryons are in stars and the interstellar medium within galaxies,â the researchers wrote in the study. The interstellar
medium
is the space between star systems.
Previous research suggested that much of the remaining baryonic matter was gas spread throughout the intergalactic mediumâthe space between galaxies. But because âthis diffuse ionized gas is notoriously difficult to measure,â the team added, scientists couldnât confirm how much of the gas existed or exactly where it was.
In the new study, the researchers relied on FRBsâquick, bright radio signals from faraway galaxies. FRBs slow down when they travel through intergalactic gas. By measuring this decrease in speed, the team could infer how much gas the signal had traversed. They investigated 60 FRBs ranging from a galaxy 11.74 million light years away to one approximately 9.1 billion light years away. The latter emitted the most distant FRB known to science, designated FRB 20230521B.
By studying FRBs, scientists confirmed that around 76% of all baryonic matter exists in the IGM, 15% in galaxy halos, and another small fraction in stars or cold galactic gas. Cosmological simulations had previously suggested this distribution, but the recent study provides direct evidence, shedding light on the movement of matter across the universe.
“Baryons are pulled into galaxies by gravity, but supermassive black holes and exploding stars can blow them back outâlike a cosmic thermostat cooling things down if the temperature gets too high,” said Connor, who is the lead author of the study. “Our results show this feedback must be efficient, blasting gas out of galaxies and into the IGM.”
“We’re beginning to see the Universe’s structure and composition in a whole new light, thanks to FRBs,â added Caltech astronomer and co-author Vikram Ravi. âThese brief flashes allow us to trace the otherwise invisible matter that fills the vast spaces between galaxies.”
With increasingly powerful telescopes expected to detect thousands of FRBs, who knows what other mysteries might soon come to light?

data.title: Show HN: Canine – A Heroku alternative built on Kubernetes
data.author: czhu12
data.article_summary: Canine是一个简化Kubernetes集群部署的平台，结合了Kubernetes的强大功能和Heroku的简洁性。它提供直观的部署体验，要求使用Docker v24.0.0或更高版本以及Docker Compose v2.0.0或更高版本。安装可通过一键脚本或手动克隆仓库并使用Docker Compose启动。Canine Cloud提供额外功能，如GitHub集成、团队协作、实时指标跟踪和简化的维护。更多信息和定价可在其官网查看。该项目基于Apache-2.0许可证，主要使用Ruby、CSS、HTML等语言开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Canine.sh作为Heroku替代方案的讨论，包括其功能、使用场景、技术细节和市场定位。

不同观点：
• [TheTaytay] 对Canine的Kubernetes文档表示赞赏，但对如何在自有基础设施上使用Canine存在疑问。他关心Canine是否能与现有Kubernetes集群集成，以及集群的构建方式（单机或多机）。
  - 问题1：在Hetzner上创建的“集群”是单机分割还是多机集群？
  - 问题2：在其他服务器上运行安装脚本是否能加入集群？
  - 问题3：是否可以利用现有的托管Kubernetes进行部署？

• [nwienert] 对Canine表示支持，但认为“为什么不应使用Canine”部分的讽刺语气适得其反，建议直接说明产品的局限性，如需要自行管理服务器、产品尚处于早期阶段等。

• [serial_dev] 认为如果需要了解Kubernetes及其相关工具（如Helm charts），Canine就不能算作真正的Heroku替代品，强调易用性和快速部署的重要性。

• [conqrr] 寻找介于Docker和Kubernetes之间的解决方案，对Canine能否真正简化Kubernetes的使用表示关注，并质疑是否仍需深入了解Kubernetes。

• [matus_congrady] 从市场角度分析Canine，认为其与Heroku对比不恰当，指出Canine在开发者体验和功能完整性上难以匹敌Heroku，尤其在生产环境中的可靠性和扩展性方面。

补充讨论：
• [vanillax] 指出Kubernetes并不仅运行Docker容器，而是符合OCI标准的容器，纠正了项目描述中的潜在误解。
• [czhu12] 分享了使用Canine搭建个人技术栈的积极体验，强调了自主管理技术基础设施的满足感。
• [debarshri] 提供了PaaS平台的维护列表，为寻找类似解决方案的用户提供了额外资源。
• [reconnecting] 关注Canine网站上的许可证信息不一致问题，要求澄清实际使用的许可证。
• [RamRodification] 指出了Kubernetes教程中的潜在笔误，体现了用户对文档质量的关注。
• [rcarmo] 对存储和密钥管理表示关注，并询问了私有代码和镜像的处理方式，强调了实际使用中的复杂性。
• [tonyhart7] 认为Canine与Kubero相似，并指出Kubero未能获得关注，暗示市场需求可能偏好更简单的工具如Coolify。
• [indigodaddy] 请求更详细的单机部署教程，表明现有视频对自托管用户不够友好。

争议焦点：
• Canine是否真正简化了Kubernetes的使用，使其成为Heroku的替代品。
• 许可证信息的不一致可能导致的法律和使用问题。
• 市场定位的合理性及与Heroku等成熟平台的实际可比性。

总体而言，讨论围绕Canine的功能、易用性、技术细节及市场定位展开，反映了不同用户对其作为Heroku替代方案的可行性及实用性的多样看法。

data.title: How to use Prometheus to efficiently detect anomalies at scale
data.author: ekiauhce
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Grafana Labs如何利用Prometheus构建一个高效的异常检测框架，以快速识别大规模系统中的异常情况。该框架基于PromQL，旨在不依赖外部系统的情况下，与Grafana Mimir等Prometheus兼容的后端无缝协作。其核心设计原则包括：无需外部系统、能够大规模高效运行、以及透明可解释。

作者详细描述了如何利用z分数公式建立基线，并通过Prometheus的录制规则（recording rules）实现平均值、标准差和乘数的计算。通过选择合适的时间窗口和乘数，他们成功创建了能够自适应波动的上下界带，从而有效检测异常。该框架已在Grafana Cloud Application Observability中应用，并被证明可靠实用。

44304860.article_content:
How to use Prometheus to efficiently detect anomalies at scale
Jorge Creixell
,
Manoj Acharya
•
2024-10-03
•
9 min
When you investigate an incident, context is everything.
Let’s say you’re working on-call and get pinged in the middle of the night. You open the alert and it sends you to a dashboard where you recognize a latency pattern. But is the spike normal for that time of day? Is it even relevant? Next thing you know, you’re expanding the time window and checking other related metrics as you try to figure out what’s going on.
It’s not to say you won’t find the answers. But time is of the essence in these scenarios, so having that context at your fingertips can be the difference between a quick resolution and a protracted trip down an incident rabbit hole.
To address this problem here at Grafana Labs, we developed an anomaly detection framework based solely on PromQL. It’s working great for us so farâboth internally for our own debugging and externally as part of
Grafana Cloud Application Observability
âand now we’re excited to share it with you!
In this blog post, which is based on
our recent PromCon talk
, we’re going to walk through how we developed this
dependable, open source framework
and how you can start putting it to use today.
How we approached building an anomaly detection framework
There are multiple ways to address anomaly detection, but we needed our framework to adhere to these principles:
No external systems.
It had to be Prometheus-compatible to work with
Grafana Mimir
. And while it’s possible to use an external tool to fetch data from Prometheus and write back to it, we wanted this to work with just the built-in Prometheus functionality so anyone can use it without needing external dependencies.
Performant at scale.
We manage all our metric data in Mimir, as well as multi-tenant instances for our Grafana Cloud users, so we needed the framework to operate at a very high scale.
No magic.
It had to be something we could explain to each other and the rest of our coworkers. It also needed to be something we could confidently trust to do the job.
These were our constraints, but we think this approach will resonate with a wider audience than just Grafana Labs. In fact, the framework will work with any Prometheus-compatible metrics backend.
Establishing baselines: a first attempt
We began with the same formula (based on the
z-score formula
) that most everyone starts with for anomaly detection:
Baselines = average Â± stddev * multiplier
This formula is so popular because it helps establish a middle lineâtypically a moving average that follows your trendsâand define the upper and lower bands of behavior so that everything outside those bands is considered an anomaly.
To implement this, we used Prometheus
recording rules
. Let’s look briefly at how we defined each component.
Average
Selecting the time window was the biggest choice we had to make here, since there’s a tradeoff between how much your middle line is lagging behind your metric and the smoothing factor you have to apply.
We found that one hour was the sweet spot, as the system is tuned for short-term anomaly detection (large deviations in small time frames). Here’s how we applied that recording rule:
Copy
- record: avg_1h
expr: avg_over_time(metric[1h])
Standard deviation
Prometheus has a
std_over_time
function, and we chose a larger time window here so we could incorporate as much information as possible to come up with bands that actually adapt to fluctuations in your metric:
Copy
- record: stddev_26h
expr: stddev_over_time(metric[26h])
We typically use 24 hours for these types of things, but we chose 26 instead to give users a bit more headroom. For example, if you have something that happens every 24 hours, you might get strange patterns where your bands start contracting or expanding. Or maybe it’s Daylight Savings Time, and the organic patterns shift as a result. The extra two hours gives us the buffer so we get more accurate predictions.
Multiplier and final formula
The multiplier is part of the tuning parameters: a higher number results in wider bands and less sensitivity, while a lower number would lead to more sensitivity. The typical multiplier is two or three, depending on the use case, and we found two was the best fit here.
Copy
- record: stddev_multiplier
expr: 2
Taken together, here is how we expressed that initial formula as a recording rule:
Copy
- record: upper_band_st
expr: avg_1h + stddev_26h * on() group_left stddev_multiplier
Note:
When you do multiplication in Prometheus, it will try to match the labels on the left and right sides. We use
group_left
to tell Prometheus to ignore labels since we don’t have any on the right side of the equation.

主要讨论点：GitHub服务状态及相关问题

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如carstonh、poly2it）报告无法访问GitHub及其支持页面，并提到在不同地区（如瑞典）也遇到了同样的问题。
• 部分用户（如josheppinette、kunagi7）具体描述了遇到的HTTP 503错误，指出某些GitHub API和网站功能无法正常使用。
• 用户andenacitelli提到GitHub的状态页面更新了关于GitHub Copilot性能下降的警告，表明GitHub已经意识到问题。
• 用户treefry和rankam指出，自UTC时间19:36和19:40起，监控实例和GitHub Actions功能出现问题。

补充讨论：
• 用户geoka9和ChrisArchitect提供了GitHub状态页面的链接，帮助其他用户获取官方状态信息。
• 用户asveikau提到一些状态网页显示正常，但个人仍然遇到了问题，暗示状态网页可能不够准确。
• 用户quicksnap引用了DownDetector网站，确认存在问题。
• 用户rmujica特别提到无法使用GitHub身份验证功能。
• 用户Hamuko报告在芬兰可以正常使用，但在欧盟其他地区收到问题反馈，表明问题可能具有地域性差异。

争议焦点：
• 官方状态页面与其他监测工具（如DownDetector）之间的信息不一致，导致用户对问题范围和严重性产生困惑。

data.title: Benzene at 200
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 苯分子在1825年由迈克尔·法拉第首次分离出来，其独特的性质使其在多个领域得到广泛应用。苯具有稳定的芳香结构，尽管高度不饱和却表现出异常的稳定性，这使其成为有机化学中芳香族化合物研究的核心。苯不仅是许多复杂分子的基础，还在健康、能源、材料、电子、食品、染料和生物技术等领域有重要应用。苯的环状结构启发了多环芳烃（PAHs）的研究，这些化合物具有独特的电子和光学性质。苯的合成衍生出了如纳米石墨烯和石墨烯等先进材料，石墨烯尤为突出，它是苯多功能性的极致体现，具有优异的导电性和强度。苯的发现和研究推动了化学和材料科学的巨大进展。

• 个人经历在苯接触和泄漏事件中的具体影响，以及这些经历如何塑造了对苯的看法和态度。

• 苯的危险性和其在工业及历史应用中的重要性之间的平衡。
• 文章在介绍苯时是否充分强调了其毒性和对健康的潜在危害。

By

Celebrating the molecule that changed the world
Source: © Shutterstock
First isolated by Michael Faraday 200 years ago, benzene’s properties have been exploited across many different fields
In 1825, Michael Faraday discovered one of the most fascinating compounds in chemistry:
benzene
. While isolating the components of oily residues of illuminating gas, Faraday identified a mysterious liquid, with a peculiar aromatic smell, which would go on to transform the landscape of chemistry.
Within the pages of the
Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London
, Faraday
described
this seemingly simple yet profoundly unique molecule. What set benzene apart, even in its earliest discovery, was its resistance to easy chemical classification. Its peculiar behaviour, such as its surprising stability despite being highly unsaturated, hinted at a deeper mystery that would not be fully resolved until the mid-19th century with the proposal of its cyclic structure.
Benzene’s physical properties only added to its mystique. This colourless liquid emitted a faintly sweet, intoxicating aroma – a hallmark of aromatic compounds. With a boiling point of 80.1°C, it was volatile and highly flammable, making it both a chemical curiosity and a potential industrial tool. Early chemists were captivated by its ability to dissolve fats, oils and other nonpolar substances, which made it a valuable solvent for experimentation and industrial processes. Yet, it was benzene’s chemical properties – its reactivity and stability – that would become the cornerstone of an entire branch of organic chemistry: aromatic compounds.
Today, benzene is everywhere, interwoven into the structures of more complex molecules that enhance our daily lives in fields as diverse as health, energy, advanced materials, electronics, food, dyes and biotechnology. This humble molecule opened the doors to a vast universe of aromatic compounds and an endless array of applications that have redefined our world.
Stability and tunability
Following benzene’s legacy came polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), a fascinating class of organic molecules composed of fused benzene rings. These structures not only preserve benzene’s aromatic stability, thanks to their electron delocalisation, but also exhibit unique electronic and optical properties determined by their size and arrangement. While smaller PAHs, like
naphthalene
and anthracene, had been characterised in the 19th century, the discovery of larger, more complex systems unveiled entirely new and surprising properties – from discrete energy levels in simpler molecules to semiconducting behaviours in larger systems like pentacene.
The synthesis and study of these compounds paved the way for nanographenes, opening new dimensions in chemistry and materials science. Through meticulous control over their molecular structures, researchers have learned to design advanced materials with tunable properties, such as electron conductivity, fluorescence, chirality and chemical reactivity. This painstaking precision highlights the intrinsic beauty of chemistry at its most fundamental level, an art of exactitude that continues to push the boundaries of possibility.
A landmark achievement in this journey was the discovery of hexabenzocoronene (HBC), in 1958. This molecule, composed of 42 carbon atoms forming 13 hexagonal rings in a perfectly flat structure, remained the largest fully characterised polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon for decades. Yet the creativity of organic chemistry knows no bounds. Klaus Müllen, a pioneer in the exploration of nanographenes, succeeded in 2002 in synthesising a remarkable structure formed by 222 carbon atoms with a diameter of 3nm, demonstrating the immense potential of organic synthesis to construct tailor-made graphene molecules.
Graphene stands out as the ultimate expression of benzene’s versatility
The fusion of benzene rings has given rise to some of the most remarkable materials in modern science, including fullerenes and carbon nanotubes. Fullerenes, often referred to as
buckyballs
, are spherical molecules composed entirely of carbon atoms arranged in a pattern of hexagons and pentagons, resembling a molecular soccer ball. These structures, discovered in 1985, owe their stability and symmetry to the aromaticity derived from benzene-like rings. Similarly, carbon nanotubes – long, cylindrical structures composed of fused aromatic rings – have captivated scientists with their extraordinary strength, flexibility and electrical conductivity. Both fullerenes and nanotubes exemplify the limitless potential of carbon chemistry, with benzene as the foundational building block.

data.title: Andrej Karpathy – Software 2.0
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary:
Andrej Karpathy在文章《Software 2.0》中提出，神经网络不仅仅是机器学习工具箱中的一个工具，而是代表了软件开发的根本性转变，称之为Software 2.0。传统的Software 1.0由人类编写明确指令的代码（如Python、C++），而Software 2.0则通过抽象的网络权重表示，无需人类直接编写代码。其开发过程依赖于数据集和神经网络架构，通过训练来填充权重，类似于编译过程。

这种新范式正在改变软件开发方式，越来越多的实际应用从1.0转向2.0。例如，视觉识别、语音识别、语音合成和机器翻译等领域，传统方法逐渐被神经网络取代。这种转变的核心在于，收集数据比编写明确程序更容易，且Software 2.0在性能和适应性上具有显著优势。Karpathy认为，软件正在吞噬世界，而AI（Software 2.0）正在吞噬软件。

Software 2.0
Andrej Karpathy
Follow
9 min read
·
Nov 11, 2017
--
179
Listen
Share
I sometimes see people refer to neural networks as just “another tool in your machine learning toolbox”. They have some pros and cons, they work here or there, and sometimes you can use them to win Kaggle competitions. Unfortunately, this interpretation completely misses the forest for the trees. Neural networks are not just another classifier, they represent the beginning of a fundamental shift in how we develop software. They are Software 2.0.
The “classical stack” of
Software 1.0
is what we’re all familiar with — it is written in languages such as Python, C++, etc. It consists of explicit instructions to the computer written by a programmer. By writing each line of code, the programmer identifies a specific point in program space with some desirable behavior.
In contrast,
Software 2.0
is written in much more abstract, human unfriendly language, such as the weights of a neural network. No human is involved in writing this code because there are a lot of weights (typical networks might have millions), and coding directly in weights is kind of hard (I tried).
Instead, our approach is to specify some goal on the behavior of a desirable program (e.g., “satisfy a dataset of input output pairs of examples”, or “win a game of Go”), write a rough skeleton of the code (i.e. a neural net architecture) that identifies a subset of program space to search, and use the computational resources at our disposal to search this space for a program that works. In the case of neural networks, we restrict the search to a continuous subset of the program space where the search process can be made (somewhat surprisingly) efficient with backpropagation and stochastic gradient descent.
To make the analogy explicit, in Software 1.0, human-engineered source code (e.g. some .cpp files) is compiled into a binary that does useful work. In Software 2.0 most often the source code comprises 1) the dataset that defines the desirable behavior and 2) the neural net architecture that gives the rough skeleton of the code, but with many details (the weights) to be filled in. The process of training the neural network compiles the dataset into the binary — the final neural network. In most practical applications today, the neural net architectures and the training systems are increasingly standardized into a commodity, so most of the active “software development” takes the form of curating, growing, massaging and cleaning labeled datasets. This is fundamentally altering the programming paradigm by which we iterate on our software, as the teams split in two: the 2.0 programmers (data labelers) edit and grow the datasets, while a few 1.0 programmers maintain and iterate on the surrounding training code infrastructure, analytics, visualizations and labeling interfaces.
It turns out that a large portion of real-world problems have the property that it is significantly easier to collect the data (or more generally, identify a desirable behavior) than to explicitly write the program. Because of this and many other benefits of Software 2.0 programs that I will go into below, we are witnessing a massive transition across the industry where of a lot of 1.0 code is being ported into 2.0 code. Software (1.0) is eating the world, and now AI (Software 2.0) is eating software.
Ongoing transition
Let’s briefly examine some concrete examples of this ongoing transition. In each of these areas we’ve seen improvements over the last few years when we give up on trying to address a complex problem by writing explicit code and instead transition the code into the 2.0 stack.
Visual Recognition
used to consist of engineered features with a bit of machine learning sprinkled on top at the end (e.g., an SVM). Since then, we discovered much more powerful visual features by obtaining large datasets (e.g. ImageNet) and searching in the space of Convolutional Neural Network architectures. More recently, we don’t even trust ourselves to hand-code the architectures and we’ve begun
searching over those
as well.
Speech recognition
used to involve a lot of preprocessing, gaussian mixture models and hidden markov models, but
today
consist almost entirely of neural net stuff. A very related, often cited humorous quote attributed to Fred Jelinek from 1985 reads “Every time I fire a linguist, the performance of our speech recognition system goes up”.
Speech synthesis
has historically been approached with various stitching mechanisms, but today the state of the art models are large ConvNets (e.g.
WaveNet
) that produce raw audio signal outputs.
Machine Translation
has usually been approaches with phrase-based statistical techniques, but neural networks are quickly becoming dominant. My favorite architectures are trained in the
multilingual setting
, where a single model translates from any source language to any target language, and in weakly supervised (or entirely
unsupervised
) settings.
Games.

44301846.article_summary:
Andrej Karpathy在文章《Software 2.0》中提出，神经网络不仅仅是机器学习工具箱中的一个工具，而是代表了软件开发的根本性转变，称之为Software 2.0。传统的Software 1.0由人类编写明确指令的代码（如Python、C++），而Software 2.0则通过抽象的网络权重表示，无需人类直接编写代码。其开发过程依赖于数据集和神经网络架构，通过训练来填充权重，类似于编译过程。

这种新范式正在改变软件开发方式，越来越多的实际应用从1.0转向2.0。例如，视觉识别、语音识别、语音合成和机器翻译等领域，传统方法逐渐被神经网络取代。这种转变的核心在于，收集数据比编写明确程序更容易，且Software 2.0在性能和适应性上具有显著优势。Karpathy认为，软件正在吞噬世界，而AI（Software 2.0）正在吞噬软件。

data.title: GitHub API Is Down
data.author: carstonh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub服务状态及Copilot依赖问题

不同观点：
• [mholt] 表示无法合并PR（Pull Request）或运行Actions，并提到根据GitHub的状态页面，这些服务似乎都需要依赖Copilot。他提供了状态页面的链接，表明问题可能与Copilot相关。

• [ColinWright] 提到大部分相关评论可以在一个特定的讨论链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44303052）中找到，暗示该链接的讨论涵盖了当前问题。

• [bluesnowmonkey] 认为当前讨论是重复的，并引用了同样的讨论链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44303052），表示该链接已经包含了相关内容。

• [andenacitelli] 指出在同一个讨论链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44303052）中有一些讨论，并且该链接的讨论似乎发布得更早，暗示它是主要讨论的源头。

补充讨论：
• 所有评论者都提到了同一个讨论链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44303052），表明该链接的讨论可能是主要讨论集中的地方。
• 争议的焦点似乎在于GitHub服务状态和Copilot依赖之间的关系，尤其是这些服务是否真的需要Copilot才能正常运行。
• 另一个值得注意的点是讨论的重复性问题，多个评论者提到当前讨论与另一个链接中的讨论重复，这可能导致信息分散和冗余。

总结：评论主要围绕GitHub服务状态以及这些服务是否需要Copilot展开，并指向了另一个讨论链接作为主要讨论的集中地。争议点在于服务的依赖关系和讨论的重复性。

data.title: Facebook announces that all videos on its platform will soon be shared as reels
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: Facebook宣布，所有视频将很快以Reels形式分享，无论长度或方向如何。视频标签将更名为Reels标签，现有视频和Reels上传选项将合并，用户不再需要选择格式。Reels将不再受长度和格式限制，默认设置也将统一。虽然这简化了发布流程，但可能导致一些用户不便，比如横屏视频被转为竖屏。Facebook表示，这一变化将逐步全球推广，视频推荐不受影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频格式和用户体验

不同观点：
• [反对混合视频格式] DoctorOW认为，将横向视频上传到竖向的Reels格式可能会很烦人，因为横向视频在竖屏展示中看起来很糟糕，影响用户体验。
• [对长视频的排斥] DoctorOW暗示用户可能不愿意在短视频中看到长视频内容，认为这会破坏观看体验。

补充讨论：
• [对平台解决方案的期待] DoctorOW阅读文章的目的是为了看看是否有任何缓解这些问题的方案，表明用户对平台优化有期望，希望平台能解决格式不匹配和视频长度不一致的问题。
• [具体例子] DoctorOW特别提到横向视频在竖屏展示中的截图效果很差，提供了一个具体的视觉体验上的论据。

44302893.article_content:
Facebook
announced
on Tuesday that all videos on its platform will soon be shared as reels, regardless of their length or orientation. Up until now, users have been able to share both video posts and reels. The company is also renaming the “Video” tab on its platform to the “Reels” tab. The update won’t change what videos are recommended to you, Facebook says.
In the coming months, users won’t have to choose between uploading a video or reel, as it will automatically be shared as a reel. In addition, reels on Facebook won’t be bound by length or format restrictions. (Currently, reels on Facebook can only be 90 seconds long.)
The idea behind the changes is to streamline the video-sharing format on the social network. It won’t be the first time that a Meta-owned platform has done so, as Instagram
began automatically
converting new video posts under 15 minutes into reels back in 2022.
“Previously, you’d upload a video to Feed or post a reel using different creative flows and tools for each format,” Facebook explained in a blog
post
. “Now, we’re bringing these experiences together with a simplified publishing flow that gives you access to even more creative tools. We’ll also give you control over your audience setting of who sees your reels.”
Image Credits:
Facebook
The change is likely to upset some users, as it may pose some challenges.
For example, it could be annoying to post a horizontal video if it gets uploaded into a vertical reels format. Plus, users may not want to see longer videos mixed in with short ones.
As part of the change, users’ default settings will now be the same for the Feed and reels. When users start to post reels after the change, they will be prompted to confirm their audience setting to determine who can see their reels: everyone, their friends, or a select group of people.

data.title: WhatsApp introduces ads in its app
data.author: greenburger
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：WhatsApp引入广告及其影响，用户隐私和数据安全问题，以及向付费服务模式的讨论。

不同观点：
• [yakkomajuri] 认为WhatsApp在巴西几乎无处不在，用户很难迁移到其他平台，比如Signal。即使Signal提供了更好的隐私保护，但由于网络效应，大多数人仍会留在WhatsApp上，即使他们可能并不关心隐私问题。这种依赖性让用户感到无力。

• [mrtksn] 提出了一种更广泛的批评，认为当前“免费”服务模式实际上是通过牺牲用户隐私和注意力来为第三方创造收入。主张回归付费服务模式，认为这样可以提升用户体验并保护隐私。

• [b0a04gl] 强调WhatsApp被Facebook收购后，逐渐从一个无广告的通讯工具转变为Meta的注意力经济工具。用户大多不会因为这些变化而迁移，因此Meta可以继续收紧控制，用户甚至可能不会注意到这些变化，直到无法逆转。

• [elric] 呼吁建立一个联合的通讯工具，认为现有的邮件和去中心化工具（如XMPP和Matrix）存在各种问题，未能提供理想的解决方案。同时，对推广这些工具的挑战表示关注。

• [crossroadsguy] 认为用户已经被逐渐“煮熟”，适应了这些变化，并质疑Signal是否会坚持其隐私保护立场，还是像其他服务一样最终妥协。

• [leokennis] 指出在荷兰，WhatsApp由于网络效应，即使引入60秒不可跳过的广告，用户也不太可能迁移到其他平台。

• [robertlagrant] 认为WhatsApp最初的无广告承诺是依靠风险投资资金实现的，并没有可持续的商业模式，因此后来的广告引入是不可避免的。

• [landhar] 对无法避免使用WhatsApp感到沮丧，因为它是主流通讯工具，但也承认这是由于其广泛的用户基础。

• [illiac786] 纠正了对WhatsApp端到端加密的误解，指出这是Meta后来引入的，并使用了Signal的代码。

• [udev4096] 预测WhatsApp引入广告将带来巨大收入，但认为转向Signal仍是一个可行的选择。

• [Daisywh] 回忆起最初选择WhatsApp是因为其无广告和加密特性，但现在感觉正在回到过去被广告充斥的老路。

• [h4kunamatata] 认为用户对大科技公司的容忍度很高，即使引入了很多不必要的功能和广告，用户也大多会继续使用。只有当问题直接影响到他们的利益时，用户才会反抗。

• [tecleandor] 提到WhatsApp在引入广告后，很快就开始向用户索取电子邮件地址，以“提高安全性”。

• [imiric] 提供了实用的安全建议，建议在单独设备上使用WhatsApp，并采取额外措施保护隐私，以应对潜在的追踪风险。

补充讨论：
• WhatsApp的网络效应使得用户难以迁移到其他平台，即使他们不满意平台的变化。
• 对广告引入及其对用户体验的影响存在广泛担忧。
• 讨论了对隐私保护的关注，以及转向Signal等替代方案的潜在可行性。
• 对去中心化和联合通讯工具的需求和挑战进行了探讨。
• 对当前“免费”服务模式的批评，以及回归付费模式的建议。

data.title: Is gravity just entropy rising? Long-shot idea gets another look
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了一个新颖的观点：重力可能并非基本力，而是熵（即无序度）增加的结果。这一理论称为“熵力重力理论”，认为物体的运动是由微观层面的随机相互作用引起的，类似于热力学中的熵增过程。尽管这一观点并非主流，且存在争议，但它提供了一种解释重力现象的新视角，并与黑洞和量子力学的研究有相似之处。该理论还具备可实验验证的潜力，因此吸引了一些物理学家的关注。文章还提到，尽管爱因斯坦的广义相对论成功解释了重力，但它在黑洞中心等极端情况下失效，表明需要更深层次的物理学解释。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： entropic gravity（熵力引力）理论及其相关类比和争议

不同观点：
• abetusk将entropic gravity与"巴西坚果效应"类比，认为大质量物体之间的引力是由于粒子撞击的密度差异造成的，但同时承认该理论的一些假设难以验证。
• MathMonkeyMan认为entropic gravity提供了一个有趣的框架，但理论中的假设过多，且与爱因斯坦场方程的联系尚不明确。
• pif作为实验物理学家，持谨慎态度，强调只有当理论能解释可观察现象时才会认可它。
• meindnoch质疑熵作为物理实体的存在，认为熵只是人类用来描述系统无知的度量，因此不能作为引力等基本力的基础。
• fnordpiglet支持entropic gravity，并将其与量子泡沫联系起来，认为这不仅能解释引力，还能解释宇宙膨胀现象。
• the__alchemist将entropic gravity与生物系统中的疏水相互作用类比，认为这是一种倾向性的统计结果。
• bawana从宇宙膨胀的角度讨论熵，提出如果宇宙膨胀速度超过其组分重新分布的速度，熵可能会减少，从而引力也会随时间变化。
• Caelus9对entropic gravity持开放态度，但指出该理论尚未提供与广义相对论不同的明确预测。
• raindeer2好奇entropic gravity是否与Wolfram的基于超图的物理模型兼容。
• colanderman以游戏中的虚拟现象为例，幽默地说明了类似熵力引力的现象。
• hoseja将其比作浮力。
• dist-epoch讨论了太阳低熵光子的来源，并将其与引力相关联。
• deadbabe提出引力可能是由于大质量物体的框架拖曳效应导致的，但这一观点缺乏普遍认可。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于熵是否可以作为引力等基本力的基础，以及entropic gravity理论的假设和验证问题。
• 不同评论者通过各种类比（如巴西坚果效应、疏水相互作用、浮力、虚拟游戏现象）来解释或质疑entropic gravity的合理性。
• 一些评论者强调了实验证据和可观察现象对理论验证的重要性。
• 对熵和宇宙膨胀关系的讨论引出了熵力引力随时间变化的可能性。

Is Gravity Just Entropy Rising? Long-Shot Idea Gets Another Look.
By
George Musser
June 13, 2025
A new argument explores how the growth of disorder could cause massive objects to move toward one another. Physicists are both interested and skeptical.

Isaac Newton was never entirely happy with his law of universal gravitation. For decades after publishing it in 1687, he sought to understand how, exactly, two objects were able to pull on each other from afar. He and others came up with several mechanical models, in which gravity was not a pull, but a push. For example, space might be filled with unseen particles that bombard the objects on all sides. The object on the left absorbs the particles coming from the left, the one on the right absorbs those coming from the right, and the net effect is to push them together.
Those theories never quite worked, and Albert Einstein eventually provided a deeper explanation of gravity as a distortion of space and time. But Einstein’s account, called general relativity,
created its own puzzles
, and he himself recognized that it could not be the final word. So the idea that gravity is a collective effect — not a fundamental force, but the outcome of swarm behavior on a finer scale — still compels physicists.
Earlier this year, a team of theoretical physicists
put forward
what might be considered a modern version of those 17th-century mechanical models. “There’s some kind of gas or some thermal system out there that we can’t see directly,” said
Daniel Carney
of Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, who led the effort. “But it’s randomly interacting with masses in some way, such that on average you see all the normal gravity things that you know about: The Earth orbits the sun, and so forth.”
This project is one of the many ways that physicists have sought to understand gravity, and perhaps the bendy space-time continuum itself, as emergent from deeper, more microscopic physics. Carney’s line of thinking, known as entropic gravity, pegs that deeper physics as essentially just the physics of heat. It says gravity results from the same random jiggling and mixing up of particles — and the attendant rise of entropy, loosely defined as disorder — that governs steam boilers, car engines and refrigerators.
Daniel Carney, a theoretical physicist at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, spearheaded the latest attempt to explain gravity as an entropic force.
The Regents of the University of California, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
Attempts at modeling gravity as a consequence of rising entropy have cropped up now and again for several decades. Entropic gravity is very much a minority view. But it’s one that won’t die, and even detractors are loath to dismiss it altogether. The new model has the virtue of being experimentally testable — a rarity when it comes to theories about the mysterious underpinnings of the universal attraction.
A Force Emerges
What makes Einstein’s theory of gravity so remarkable is not just that it works (and does so with sublime mathematical beauty), but that it betrays its own incompleteness. General relativity predicts that stars can collapse to form black holes, and that, at the centers of these objects, gravity becomes infinitely strong. There, the space-time continuum tears open like an overloaded grocery bag, and the theory is unable to say what comes next. Furthermore, general relativity has uncanny parallels to heat physics, even though not a single thermal concept went into its development. It predicts that black holes only grow, never shrink, and only swallow, never disgorge. Such irreversibility is characteristic of the flow of heat. When heat flows, energy takes a more randomized or disordered form; once it does, it is unlikely to reorder itself spontaneously. Entropy quantifies this growth of disorder.
Indeed, when physicists used quantum mechanics to study what happens in the distorted space-time around a black hole, they find that black holes give off energy like any hot body. Because heat is the random motion of particles, these thermal effects suggest to many researchers that black holes, and the space-time continuum in general, actually consist of some kind of particles or other microscopic components.

data.title: Maya Blue: Unlocking the Mysteries of an Ancient Pigment
data.author: DanielKehoe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了古玛雅文明中独特的颜料——“玛雅蓝”（Maya Blue）。这种颜料从晚期前古典时期（公元前300年到公元300年）一直使用到殖民时期，象征雨神Chaak，常用于祭祀、雕塑、陶器、壁画和抄本。玛雅蓝颜色鲜艳，耐久性强，甚至在暴露于恶劣自然环境上千年后仍保持其蓝色。文章还提到，在奇琴伊察等考古遗址中，尽管许多区域因旅游业而关闭，但仍能见到这种颜料的遗存。文章引用了考古学家Dean E. Arnold的研究，详细描述了玛雅蓝的制作及其文化意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“玛雅蓝”色素的讨论，以及由此引发的对其他古代色素的兴趣和回忆。

不同观点：
• [jihadjihad] 认为该网站设计怀旧，令人回想起20年前网络的风格，尤其是其“简陋”的设计和细节（如底部的诗和Comic Sans字体）。该评论者对旧时的网页元素如.swf文件有所怀念，表现出对过去网络风格的怀念情感。

• [NaOH] 提供了与玛雅蓝相关的其他资源链接，引用了其他讨论和文章，如“Maya blue”色素在丢失两百年后被重新创造的新闻，引导读者查看更多信息。这表明该评论者关注的是信息的扩展和相关资源的提供。

• [dclaw] 提供了具体的文章链接，说明有人已经成功 recreated 玛雅蓝色素，并给出参考资料。这显示出该评论者注重事实和具体例证，尝试补充讨论中的实际案例。

• [maxwell] 提到了另一种古代色素“埃及蓝”，通过对比其与玛雅蓝的化学成分，强调两者在成分上的显著不同。这表明该评论者关注的是不同古代色素之间的科学区别。

• [tinkertrain] 提供了一个关于色素的补充资源，推荐了国家美术馆的播客，特别提到了其中一集关于普鲁士蓝的历史，为对色素感兴趣的读者提供了额外学习材料。这显示出该评论者乐于分享相关学习资源。

• [noduerme] 分享了个人经历，提到自己飞行途中看到的尤卡坦地区的水色，与玛雅蓝色素颜色相似，表达了对该色素与自然景象关联的感叹。该评论者注重个人体验和与现实世界的联系。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多种古代色素（玛雅蓝、埃及蓝、普鲁士蓝），表现出对色素历史和化学成分的广泛兴趣。
• 评论者们提供了多个外部资源链接，展示了讨论的延展性和对更多信息的渴求。
• 对网站设计的怀旧观点与其他关于色素的科学讨论形成对比，显示出讨论主题的多样性。

争议焦点：
• 讨论中并没有明显的争议，但不同评论的侧重点有所不同，如对网站设计的怀旧情感与对色素科学成分的探讨之间存在一定的张力。

Maya Blue: Unlocking the Mysteries of an Ancient Pigment
We are sincerely grateful to Dr. Dean E. Arnold for writing specially for us this intriguing introduction to the mysterious and unique pigment known as Maya Blue. Dr. Arnold has published extensively about the Maya potters and their craft in Ticul, Yucatan from data collected during his twelve visits over a period of 43 years (1965-2008). He is currently Adjunct Curator of Anthropology at the Field Museum and Professor of Anthropology Emeritus at Wheaton College (Illinois).
Pic 1: Close-up of Maya Blue on sculpture on the Venus Platform at Chichén Itzá (Click on image to enlarge)
Maya Blue is a beautiful blue pigment used by the ancient Maya from the Late Preclassic Period (300 BC - 300 AD) up into the Colonial Period (pic 1). It mimics the color of the azure sky and the turquoise of the Caribbean that one sees from the Maya Rivera - that incomparable strip of coastline that stretches along the east side of the Yucatán Peninsula.
Maya Blue was the color of sacrifice for the ancient Maya, and they painted human sacrifices, sculpture, pottery, murals, and codices with it (pic 2). Symbolizing the rain god
Chaak
, among other meanings, the Maya employed it largely during the Late Classic, Terminal Classic, and Postclassic Periods. After the Spanish Conquest, it occurred on murals in churches and convents, and there is some evidence that it was used up into the 19th century.
Pic 2: Maya Blue on a mural on the base of the Castillo at Mayapán (Click on image to enlarge)
Before the modern rush of tourism forced the closure of many parts of archaeological sites, one could still see Maya Blue on the sculpture and murals that still retained its rich blue color unchanged from the time of its creation. One archaeological site that evinces its persistent color is Chichén Itzá, an ancient Maya city on the northern Yucatán Peninsula (pic 3). As visitors walk northward from the great Pyramid of Kukulkan to a sinkhole called the ‘Sacred Well’, they encounter a low pyramidal structure known as the Venus Platform (pic 4). Careful observers will note that the low relief sculpture on it still retains some of its ancient paint. Looking closely, they can see the remains of a blue pigment, still clinging to the crumbling limestone, yet with a richness of color unfaded after a millennium of exposure to the harsh tropical sun, torrential downpours, and hurricanes that have plagued Yucatán for centuries. Although much of the pigment has disappeared because of the erosion of the limestone underneath it, that which remains still retains its bright blue color.

data.title: Strangers in the Middle of a City: The John and Jane Does of L.A. Medical Center
data.author: dangle1
data.article_summary:
文章讲述了洛杉矶综合医疗中心（L.A. General）处理无名病患的挑战。作为德州以西最繁忙的创伤中心，该医院每年接收约13万名急诊病人，其中一些因昏迷、丧失行为能力或病情严重无法提供身份信息。尽管多数无名氏患者在48小时内能被确认身份，但每年仍有几十例难以确认，滞留医院数周甚至数年。

文章具体描述了一位无名男子，他于2月6日在东好莱坞被发现后送医，无任何身份证明或通讯设备。医院通过各种途径尝试确认其身份，包括发布照片和搜索数据库，但未果。这类患者不仅带来行政管理问题，还存在医疗安全隐患，因无法得知其过敏史或用药信息。医院在保护隐私的同时，需依法寻找解决方案以确保患者获得适当治疗。

不同观点：
• [dzink] 认为医院的成本负担往往最重，这些成本最终会通过更高的费用转嫁给付费患者。这表明，当前的系统下，医院在处理身份不明患者时承受了较大的经济压力，而这些成本最终会影响所有患者的医疗费用。

• [kylehotchkiss] 提出了一种由地方检察官办公室（DA’s office）协助的解决方案。具体做法包括让警官协助识别患者身份，若患者拒绝识别身份则进行指纹采集，随后决定是否不予起诉或撤销案件。这种方法旨在通过执法部门的协助，既保护患者的权益，也帮助医院解决身份识别问题，从而降低医院的成本压力。

• [kylehotchkiss] 的方案中提到了一种折中办法，即通过执法部门的介入，但最终不进行正式起诉，以避免对患者的过度惩罚，同时解决医院面临的实际问题。这表明了一种在患者权益和医院需求之间寻找平衡的尝试。

At the busiest trauma center west of Texas, hospital staff race to identify dozens of patients who have no identification and are too ill to say who they are.
He had a buzz cut and brown eyes, a stubbly beard and a wrestler’s build.
He did not have a wallet or phone; he could not state his name. He arrived at Los Angeles General Medical Center one cloudy day this winter just as thousands of people do every year: alone and unknown.
Some 130,000 people are brought each year to L.A. General’s emergency room. Many are unconscious, incapacitated or too unwell to tell staff who they are.
Nearly all these Jane and John Does are identified within 48 hours or so of admission. But every year, a few dozen elude social workers’ determined efforts to figure out who they are.
Too sick to be discharged yet lacking the identification they need to be transferred to a more appropriate facility, they stay at L.A.’s busiest trauma hospital for weeks. Sometimes months. Occasionally years.
Advertisement
That’s an outcome no one wants. And so hospital staff did for the buzz cut man what they do once every other possibility is exhausted.
Social workers cobbled together the tiny bit of information they could legally share: his height and weight, his estimated age, his date of admission, the place where he was found. They stood over his hospital bed and took his photograph.
Then they asked the 10 million people of Los Angeles County: Does anyone know who this is?
This unidentified patient arrived at L.A. General on Feb. 6 after being found unconscious in East Hollywood.
(Los Angeles General Medical Center)

Just before 8 a.m. on Feb. 16, paramedics responded to a medical emergency at 1037  N. Vermont Ave.
The man was face-down on a stretch of sidewalk lined with chain-link fences and sandbags, near a public restroom and the entrance to the Vermont/Santa Monica subway stop. Pink scrape marks blossomed above and below his right eye.
Advertisement
Paramedics estimated he was about 30 years old. Hospital staff guessed 35 to 40.
He had no possessions that might offer clues: no phone, no wallet, no tickets or receipts crumpled in his pockets.
He could not state his name or answer any questions. The hospital admitted him under a name the English-speaking world has used for centuries when a legal name can’t be verified: John Doe.
The vast majority of patients admitted as John Does leave as themselves. The unconscious wake up. The intoxicated sober up. Frantic relatives call the hospital looking for a missing loved one, or police arrive seeking their suspect.
None of these things happened for the man from North Vermont. When he finally opened his eyes, his language was minimal: a few indistinct words — possibly English, possibly Spanish — and nothing that sounded like a name.
Social workers wrote down everything they knew for sure about their patient: his height (4 feet, 10 inches), his weight (181 pounds), the color of his eyes (dark brown).
Then they started following the trail that typically leads to identification.
The ambulance crew didn’t recognize him, and the run sheet — the document paramedics use to record patients’ condition and care — had no revelatory details.
Advertisement
They checked Google Maps. Any nearby shelter whose manager they could call to ask about a missing resident? Nope. Was there an apartment building whose residents might recognize his photo? Nothing.
A second photo L.A. General released to the public in search of a name or next of kin for this unidentified patient found in East Hollywood.
(Los Angeles General Medical Center)
They clicked through county databases. His details didn’t align with any previously admitted hospital patient, or anyone in the mental health system. No missing-persons report matched his description; social workers couldn’t find a mention of someone like him in any social media posts.
An anonymous patient is an administrative problem. It’s also a safety concern. If a patient can’t state their name, they probably also can’t say if they have life-threatening allergies or are taking any medications, said Dr. Chase Coffey, who oversees the hospital’s social work team.
“We do our darndest to deliver safe, effective, high-quality care in these scenarios, but we run into limits there,” he said.

data.title: Timescale Is Now TigerData
data.author: pbowyer
data.article_summary: 2025年6月17日，Ajay Kulkarni和Mike Freedman发表了文章《Speed Without Sacrifice: Building the Modern PostgreSQL for the Analytical and Agentic Era》。文章讨论了为分析和代理时代构建现代化PostgreSQL数据库的进展，强调在提升速度的同时不牺牲其他关键性能。该文章属于“Announcements & Releases”类别，并提供了订阅TigerData Newsletter的选项，订阅需同意其隐私政策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Timescale公司更名为TigerData及其相关技术和品牌决策的合理性与潜在问题

不同观点：
• 支持更名并认可其战略调整：
  - ethagnawl：认为更名为TigerData是有道理的，因为随着pgvectorscale的推出，原有的DB扩展支持对公司变得越来越不重要。他之前使用过pgvectorscale，并对产品和团队印象深刻。
  - justinmitchel：对更名和保留TimescaleDB等名称的决定表示赞赏。

• 对品牌更名的困惑与质疑：
  - lukaslalinsky：不理解为何要更改一个已经具有一定辨识度的品牌名称，尤其是在没有出售的情况下。
  - apgwoz：指出TigerData和TigerBeetle的名称相似，建议选择其他与“快速猫科动物”相关的名字。
  - rattray：理解公司以老虎作为吉祥物的品牌文化，但认为与其他品牌（如TigerBeetle、WiredTiger）存在名称冲突，建议选择如TiScaleDB等其他名称。

• 对具体名称选择的建议与幽默评论：
  - 8K832d7tNmiQ：建议使用TigerScale作为新名称。
  - nelsonfigueroa：庆幸公司没有在名称中加上“AI”。

• 对潜在混淆的担忧：
  - talos_：认为与Tigris Data的名称冲突更为严重，尽管Tigris没有老虎标志，但在活动中曾有老虎贴纸。
  - jeffchuber：认为TigerData和TigerGraph这两个数据库公司的名称相似，可能会导致混淆。

• 对技术层面的讨论与质疑：
  - doctoboggan：质疑InfluxDB是否被视为技术死胡同。
  - georgewfraser：回忆与Timescale CTO的技术讨论，质疑Timescale与标准列式数据库的区别，认为其可能只是另一个列式数据库管理系统。

补充讨论：
• 关于与其他技术和品牌的关联性讨论：
  - pmalynin：质疑TigerData与WiredTiger是否有任何关系。
  
• 幽默和轻松的评论：
  - jamesgresql：以“这里是Tiger，出发！”这样的幽默方式参与讨论。

争议焦点：
• 更名策略的合理性及其对品牌辨识度和市场混淆的影响。
• 技术定位的清晰性及与其他数据库技术的区别。

总结：评论中主要讨论了Timescale更名为TigerData的战略决策，包括对其品牌、技术定位的认可与质疑，以及对潜在市场混淆的担忧。同时，评论中也包含了一些对具体名称选择的建议和幽默评论。

data.title: Show HN: Lstr – A modern, interactive tree command written in Rust
data.author: w108bmg
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了用Rust编写的目录树查看工具**lstr**，其特点是快速、简约并支持交互模式。它受到命令行程序`tree`的启发，具备高性能（目录并行扫描）、经典与交互模式、丰富的信息显示（如文件图标、权限、大小）、Git集成（显示文件状态）、智能过滤（遵循`.gitignore`）等功能。用户可以通过命令行选项自定义输出，如显示所有文件（`-a`）、只显示目录（`-d`）、控制递归深度（`-L`）等。交互模式支持键盘操作，可以与工具如`fzf`结合使用进行模糊查找，或通过`less`、`bat`分页显示大目录。文章还提供了将`lstr`用作可视化`cd`命令的Shell集成方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust项目的第一印象、二进制文件大小、Rust语言的特点以及与类似工具的比较

不同观点：
• [ipdashc] 认为项目演示的GIF中使用了破损的图标，虽然很酷，但这是个大胆的选择，可能不太合适。
• [w108bmg] 对收到的反馈表示感谢，特别是关于如何缩小二进制文件大小的建议，因为这是其第一个Rust包，所以非常重视这些反馈。
• [drabbiticus] 对项目的界面表示赞赏，但惊讶于依赖树的深度，特别是url和git crate的依赖关系，并对二进制文件的大小（53M）与类似工具（如/usr/sbin/tree，80K）的巨大差异表示疑惑。后续编辑中提到通过`cargo build --release`和其他选项可以显著减小二进制文件的大小。
• [sdegutis] 对项目作者使用Rust编写项目的体验感兴趣，询问其对Rust的喜好、不喜欢之处或感到惊讶的地方。
• [aystatic] 认为该项目像是erdtree和broot的结合体，询问该项目是否有特别突出的功能区别于其他两个工具。

补充讨论：
• 关于二进制文件大小的争议焦点在于Rust项目的依赖深度和链接方式，许多依赖导致二进制文件较大，但通过特定构建选项可以减小文件大小。
• 对于Rust项目的初学者来说，依赖树的深度和构建结果的大小是常见的困惑点，社区反馈帮助解答了这些疑问。
• 与已有工具（erdtree和broot）的比较引出了该项目可能的独特功能和优势，这可能是用户选择使用该工具的重要考虑因素。

data.title: Proofs Without Words
data.author: squircle
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了“无字证明”（Proofs without words）的概念，通过图形直观展示各种数学定理和恒等式的证明。文章分为三个部分：**求和**、**几何**和**杂项**。在求和部分，展示了奇数数列、几何级数和斐波那契数列的图形证明。几何部分通过图形解释了毕达哥拉斯定理、三角形和平行四边形的面积计算等。杂项部分涉及不等式、费马小定理等内容。文章通过一系列图示和动画，帮助读者直观理解复杂的数学概念和定理。

不同观点：
• **fiforpg** 提到有一本关于几何陈述的书，书中的每个图片都代表一个事实，而证明则由读者自行补充。同时指出，书中一些陈述的证明较为困难，提醒读者注意。
   
• **jupitr** 分享了一个关于如何利用视觉证明进行误导的视频链接，意在提醒视觉化证明虽然直观，但也有可能被用来误导观众，强调了批判性看待视觉证明的必要性。

• **downboots** 推荐了一个网站，该网站对每个定理提供了简洁的一页概述，适合作为快速参考工具，突出了资源的多样性与便捷性。

• **brianberns** 介绍了自己创建的一个游戏，该游戏以无字证明为中心，鼓励通过互动和游戏化的方式学习数学证明，强调了实践与互动在学习中的重要性。

• **vonnik** 推荐了David Bessis的Mathematica一书，认为该书适合喜欢视觉化学习的人，强调了经典书籍在学习中的价值。

44275714.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了“无字证明”（Proofs without words）的概念，通过图形直观展示各种数学定理和恒等式的证明。文章分为三个部分：**求和**、**几何**和**杂项**。在求和部分，展示了奇数数列、几何级数和斐波那契数列的图形证明。几何部分通过图形解释了毕达哥拉斯定理、三角形和平行四边形的面积计算等。杂项部分涉及不等式、费马小定理等内容。文章通过一系列图示和动画，帮助读者直观理解复杂的数学概念和定理。

data.title: Incant – add magic spells to your code
data.author: montyanderson
data.article_summary: "Incant" 是一个代码库，旨在通过集成语言模型为代码添加"魔法 spells"。它提供了安全调用这些模型的基础功能，允许用户创建选择器和过滤器等操作。使用 `createSelector` 可以选取数据中的最高值，而 `createFilter` 则用于过滤特定类型的数据。所有输入数据都会被发送至上游推理服务提供商，因此建议避免传递个人敏感信息。该工具易于配置，用户可以通过环境变量（如 `OPENAI_API_KEY`）进行设置。代码示例展示了如何选择最大数字和过滤男性名字，确保输出是输入数组的子集且无虚构数据。该项目主要使用 TypeScript 编写。

总结：Marcus_holmes 主要关注“无幻觉保证”的运作方式，特别是如何处理性别中立名字，并希望该技术能够提供包含或排除性别中立名字的设置选项。他对该技术表示了初步的认可和兴趣。

data.title: 122.88TB SSD on sale for $12,399 quite a bargain – if you can afford it
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: Solidigm的122.88TB D5-P5336 SSD现已正式发售，售价为12,399美元，较最初预估的14,000美元更为实惠。该SSD采用PCIe 4.0接口，有U.2和E1.L两种规格，主要面向处理大规模AI、机器学习和数据密集型工作负载的企业存储环境。它使用192层QLC NAND，耐久度为每天0.60次全盘写入，五年内总写入量达134.3PB。性能方面，4K随机读取速度高达930,000 IOPS，顺序读取速度为7.4GBps。该SSD旨在解决数据中心的空间和功耗限制，相比传统混合系统可减少机架使用和降低功耗约90%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据中心存储方案的成本与性能比较

不同观点：
• 观点一：消费者级别的NVMe SSD可以以更低的成本构建类似容量但速度更快的存储方案。例如，carcinklko提到使用消费级NVMe M.2 SSD构建相同容量的存储系统，成本大约为6,500€（含税），而且速度更快。
  - 论据：成本具体为6,500€，并且强调速度更快。
  
• 观点二：数据中心客户可能更注重空间和电力效率。carcinklko指出，对于非常注重空间和电力效率的数据中心客户，消费者级别SSD的方案可能并不适合，因为这些客户可能对能耗和空间利用有更高的要求。
  - 论据：数据中心客户的特殊需求，如空间和电力效率。

补充讨论：
• 成本与性能的权衡：讨论涉及到不仅要考虑初始硬件成本，还要考虑性能和运营成本（如电力、空间）。
• 争议焦点：消费者级SSD是否能够在整体拥有成本和性能上与专业数据中心存储方案相媲美，尤其是在空间和电力效率方面。

这个讨论反映了在选择数据中心存储方案时，成本和性能之间的权衡以及不同客户需求对选择的影响。

Solidigm’s monster 122.88TB D5-P5336 SSD is now officially available
It's designed to meet demands of modern hyperscale data infrastructure
Initial estimates suggested $14,000, but you can order it for "just" $12,399
Originally announced in November 2024, the
122.88TB model of Solidigm’s D5-P5336 SSD
has officially gone on sale.
If you’ve ever wondered how much one of these giant-capacity SSDs might set you back, the answer is: maybe not quite as much as you’d expect, as although early estimates placed its price close to $14,000, but you can actually pick up the drive from
Tech-America
for a much more affordable $12,399.
Obviously, this isn’t a drive for your typical PC rig - it uses a PCIe 4.0 interface and comes in U.2 (available now) and E1.L (expected later this year) form factors. It’s aimed at enterprise storage environments handling large-scale AI, machine learning, and data-intensive workloads.

Longer lasting QLC
The drive is built with 192-layer QLC NAND. With endurance rated at 0.60 drive writes per day and a total of 134.3 petabytes written over five years, the 122.88TB model is designed to last longer than earlier QLC offerings.
Solidigm, a US-based subsidiary of SK Hynix, reportedly tested the drive under extreme conditions. Running 32KB random writes at full load, the drive operated continuously for five years and retained around 5 percent of its life.
Performance claims include up to 930,000 IOPS for
4K
random reads and 7.4GBps for sequential reads.
Solidigm markets its
large SSD
as a solution to space and power constraints in data centers, claiming that replacing traditional hybrid systems with its all-QLC drives could reduce rack usage from nine to one and cut power consumption by around 90 percent.

data.title: Claude Code feels like magic because it is iterative
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Claude Code工具的运作原理和实际价值。Claude Code利用迭代和启发式算法，通过多次尝试找到解决方案，从而给人一种“智能”提升的错觉。尽管基础模型未改变，但其自主尝试和快速执行能力让用户感受到更高的效率和智能化。作者通过实际测试，如自动更新项目依赖项，展示了该工具在速度和自主性方面的优势。文章还探讨了这种技术在更大规模应用中的潜力，提出若能进一步压缩任务时间，将极大提升其实用价值，并可能改变许多任务的处理方式。最终，作者对LLM（大语言模型）工具的未来应用持乐观态度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（如Claude Code）在代码代理和自动化任务中的实际效果和应用前景

不同观点：
• GardenLetter27：认为当前的LLM在处理大规模代码项目时仍然存在局限性，特别是在处理上下文和运行测试时。尽管在一些小型评估中表现良好，但错误仍然令人担忧。同时，通过更高级的LLM进行审查虽然能提高准确性，但成本过高。
• guluarte：基于个人经验，认为使用代理浪费时间和金钱，只适合处理小型任务，且需要频繁的人工干预。
• stpedgwdgfhgdd：对近期的发展印象深刻，但认为当前仍需大量人工干预。不认为大型企业的复杂项目能通过LLM迅速取得成功，特别是在测试驱动开发方面。
• bgwalter：对LLM在企业环境中的应用持怀疑态度，认为过度自动化可能导致失业。对LLM的宣传和自动化趋势表示担忧。
• lokimedes：认为当前的LLM更多是依靠蛮力计算而非真正的智能，智能应体现在更快找到最优解的能力上。
• revskill：认为LLM反映的是使用者的智能，而非其自身具备的智能。

• talles：认为技术在不理解的情况下显得像魔法。

44297349.article_content:
It takes these very simple-minded instructions - 'Go fetch a number, add it to this number, put the result there, perceive if it's greater than this other number' - but executes them at a rate of, let's say, 1,000,000 per second. At 1,000,000 per second, the results appear to be magic. — Steve Jobs
Claude Code feels like magic because it is iterative. The solution to
any
problem is random. You just have to iterate through the whole possible space until you find one that works.
Here, let me illustrate:
intelligence
=
heuristic
*
attempt
If your attempts are purely random, you need roughly the size of the search space to find a solution. A
heuristic
cuts that down significantly. That is essentially what an LLM is.
Claude Code uses the same models provided through the API or the web interface. Yet, users feel a boost in intelligence. The model didn't get smarter but because Claude Code can make several attempts on its own, its overall intelligence increases for the end user.
As LLMs performance plateaus, intelligence can be derived from the second factor. In this regard, AI tools can have value on their own.
I have been using Claude Code for the last week or so. I completely disregarded it at first because I thought a Chat window where I manually go back and forth is enough. But there is something to be gained from speed and autonomy.
New Era?
I've used LLMs extensively but remained skeptical of their practical value. Claude Code changed that perspective through one concrete test: updating dependencies on a project with compilation and extensive tests. The tool iterated back and forth dozens of times over 30-40 minutes. I intervened occasionally, but mostly watched it work.
Consider the implications of scale. What if Claude Code operated autonomously with massive parallel compute? Could it compress that 40-minute task into 10 minutes? 5 minutes? 1 minute?
If 1 minute proves to be feasible, is it possible to go back to the old way of updating dependencies? What about other tasks? What other tasks could be automated
today
with the current LLMs performance?

data.article_summary: 香港传统中药公司Regencell Bioscience的股价在短短八周内暴涨超过82,000%，使其创始人欧弋锴的净资产飙升至约333亿美元，跻身全球最富有行列。该公司主要研发和授权由欧弋锴父亲欧石吉开发的治疗多动症和自闭症的中药配方，目前仍处于研发阶段，未实现盈利。2024财年净亏损440万美元。尽管如此，公司市值已从一年前的5300万美元增至约387亿美元。近期，公司实施了38比1的股票拆分，股价一度暴涨434%。欧弋锴自小患有ADHD和阅读障碍，但仍成功进入加州大学伯克利分校，并曾在德意志银行工作。他的兄弟欧弋鹏是房地产投资公司Veritas的创始人，财富超过1亿美元。

A blistering rally in a tiny, money-losing traditional Chinese medicine company’s stock has vaulted its founder’s net worth to among the world’s largest fortunes.
The firm, Hong Kong-based Regencell Bioscience, was for all intents and purposes trading as a microcap stock on the Nasdaq just eight weeks ago. But its shares have since exploded, gaining more than 82,000 per cent since its February 13 low. The move has boosted the value of chief executive officer Yat-Gai Au’s 86 per cent stake to $US33.3 billion ($51.4 billion), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, making Au’s paper wealth greater than rich-list stalwarts such as Phil Knight and Masayoshi Son.
Shares of the company have been on a bizarre tear in 2025, with little to no news from the firm.
Credit:
Bloomberg
The shares closed up 30 per cent to $US78 in New York trading, after gaining 283 per cent on Monday following a 38-for-1 stock split.
The unbelievable rally has transformed Regencell Bioscience Holdings, a penny stock as recently as April, to one worth around $US38.7 billion in market value. A year ago, the company had a market capitalisation of $US53 million. This is despite having a net loss of $US4.4 million for its fiscal year that ended June 2024, a 28 per cent decrease from the previous year.
Regencell is an improbable vehicle for creating a multibillion-dollar fortune. Largely self-funded by Au, the company sells herbal medicine treatments for ADHD and autism spectrum disorder. The firm is still in the R&D phase and has never turned a profit since going public, losing $US4.4 million in the fiscal year through June 30, 2024, according to filings. Its chief medical officer position has been vacant since the last doctor to hold the job resigned in 2022.
“Both entities [Regencell and its associated foundation] are Gai’s passion projects, and he will continue to invest his personal funds to defend what he believes in,” according to Au’s bio page on the company’s website. “He has literally put his money where his mouth is by investing over US$9 million in RGC to demonstrate his personal belief and commitment.”
Loading
Family business
Founded in 2014, Regencell’s main line of business is marketing and licensing traditional treatments developed by the founder’s father, Sik-Kee Au. The elder Au has a background in electrical engineering and formerly owned a security alarm business in California. In August 2021, he was found guilty of professional misconduct by a practitioners’ board in Hong Kong for overprescribing medicine, according to a public order.
Advertisement
Regencell has exclusive rights over traditional medicinal formulas developed by Sik-Kee Au trademarked under the name Brain Theory. They consist of liquid-based herbal compounds taken twice daily, aimed at treating neurocognitive disorders.
Yat-Gai Au’s net worth has soared.
Credit:
Regencell
The younger Au started Regencell after he was diagnosed with ADHD as a child and suffered from dyslexia through much of his schooling. Despite those learning difficulties, he attended the Haas School of Business at the University of California-Berkeley and landed a job at Deutsche Bank AG in the late 1990s, working on more than $US4 billion in deals before founding Regencell.
His older brother Yat-Pang is the founder and CEO of Veritas Investments, a property investment company that manages roughly 250 buildings on the US West Coast. In 2019, Bloomberg valued his wealth at more than $100 million.
As a high schooler growing up in Silicon Valley, Yat-Pang made headlines as a symbol of alleged anti-Asian discrimination in college admissions when he was rejected from UC Berkeley despite an excellent academic record, according to a 1987
Los Angeles Times
report. He later went on earn an MBA from Harvard Business School in 2000.
The improbable surge
Regencell Bioscience this month said its board approved a 38-for-1 stock split. When the split took effect, shares rose as much as 434 per cent – their biggest one-day jump ever – to a record high, triggering more than 10 volatility halts.
Shares of the company have been on a bizarre tear in 2025, with little to no news released. The Hong Kong-based company, which debuted on the Nasdaq Capital Market in 2021, is in the research and development stage and has not generated any revenue since inception, according to its most-recent annual filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
The company says its traditional Chinese medicine formula contains only natural ingredients.
Credit:
Internet
A representative for Regencell didn’t immediately respond to a Bloomberg request for comment.

data.article_summary: 《星际穿越》（Interstellar）是一部2014年上映的科幻冒险电影，由克里斯托弗·诺兰（Christopher Nolan）执导，诺兰与其兄弟乔纳森共同编剧。影片讲述了在未来地球不再适宜居住的情况下，前NASA飞行员库珀（马修·麦康纳饰）带领团队前往外太空寻找新家园的故事。电影时长169分钟，预算1.65亿美元，全球票房达7.58亿美元。主要演员包括安妮·海瑟薇（饰布兰德）和杰西卡·查斯坦等。影片获得IMDb 8.7的高分评价，并融合了冒险、科幻和情感等多重元素。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新数据库与IMDB和TMDB的比较及功能

不同观点：
• [vivzkestrel] 提问新数据库与IMDB和TMDB相比如何，关注点在于新数据库的特色、功能和差异性。

• [darkotodoric] 回应并介绍了该新数据库的特点：
  1. 数据来源多样，经过格式化和系统组织。
  2. 数据每天更新，部分数据甚至一天更新多次，保证时效性。
  3. 提供每月1000次请求的免费API包。
  4. 计划创建开源脚本，支持在JellyFin、Plex上自动更新数据，并与Radarr和Sonarr集成，自动下载电影和剧集。

补充讨论：
• [darkotodoric] 积极征求用户的建议和批评，显示出对用户反馈的开放态度。
• 争议焦点可能在于新数据库能否在功能和数据质量上与已经非常成熟的IMDB和TMDB竞争，尤其是在用户习惯和社区信任方面。
• 另一个值得注意的点是，新数据库提供的自动化功能（如与JellyFin、Plex、Radarr、Sonarr的集成）可能成为其吸引特定用户群（如家庭媒体服务器用户）的重要优势。

主要讨论点：自动结账技术与商业模式的应用及其潜在影响

不同观点：
• [wormius] 认为时间就是金钱，便利性可以转化为经济价值。他提出了一种商业模式，即通过支付少量费用，消费者可以选择提前解锁获取商品，强调了时间与金钱的转换关系。这是一种“付费加速”的模式，可能应用于自助购物场景中。

• [dtagames] 支持这种技术在美国的应用，并提到此类技术已经在欧洲广泛使用。他指出，这种技术更合理的应用场景是为即将过期或未售出的商品提供折扣，而不是提高商品价格。他还提到，在当今比价网站和应用程序普及的情况下，商店更倾向于展示低价，而非提高价格。此外，打印和丢弃大量货架标签是种浪费，电子标签等技术则可以减少这种浪费。

• [4d4m] 持怀疑态度，简单表示"尚未"看到这种技术在美国普及，暗示对该技术在美国实施的可行性或接受度存在质疑。

补充讨论：
• [dtagames] 提到了环保和效率问题，认为自动结账和电子标签等技术可以减少纸张浪费，具有环保意义。同时，他还指出了现代消费者比价行为对商家定价策略的影响，进一步讨论了这种技术对商业运营的实际作用。

• 争议焦点在于这种技术是否能被广泛接受，尤其是在不同市场（如美国与欧洲）之间的差异。同时，对于付费提前解锁商品的商业模式，也存在接受度和可行性的讨论。

data.title: What happens when clergy take psilocybin
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了十多位宗教领袖参与一项实验，服用迷幻蘑菇（含裸盖菇素）的经历。尽管实验初期因伦理问题和资金来源争议被延迟公布，最终发表在《迷幻医学》期刊上的结果显示，超过90%的参与者认为这次体验是他们一生中最具精神意义和神圣的经历之一，近一半人认为这是他们经历过最深刻的事情。尽管实验存在样本偏小、参与者背景单一等问题，结果仍引发了对迷幻药物与宗教体验关系的讨论。一些宗教领袖甚至因此更加开放，将迷幻体验融入自己的宗教教导中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： psychedelics（尤其是LSD和迷幻蘑菇）的精神性、适用性、以及它们与宗教和科学的关联。

不同观点：
• [gchamonlive] 认为LSD可以带来精神性的体验，帮助个人深入了解自我和存在的本质，但同时强调这种体验并不适合所有人。他指出，个体需要具备一定的哲学和心理准备来应对这些体验，并且每个人的旅程都是独特的。

• [WastedCucumber] 警告有精神病或精神分裂症家族史的人不应接触迷幻药物，尤其是如果他们曾经在使用大麻或其他药物时感到偏执。他们建议这些人尝试冥想等其他方式。

• [SlowTao] 引用Ram Dass的话，提到1960年代的LSD研究中，实验参与者的反应非常明显，不同的人有截然不同的体验，有些甚至出现了极端的精神体验。

• [stared] 推荐《Sacred Knowledge》一书，认为该书通过科学研究探讨了迷幻药物与宗教体验的关系，并指出无论是否宗教信仰者，阅读后都会对这一话题有新的思考。

• [nathan_compton] 表示自己多次使用LSD和Psilocybin，但从未感受到所谓的精神性体验，并对人们谈论的精神体验感到困惑。

• [alex-vlasis] 分享了自己作为穆斯林背景的人使用LSD的体验，认为这种体验与宗教主题有共鸣，包括先知感、内心平和、对死亡的接受、音乐的神圣感以及对善恶哲学的重新思考。

• [throw18376] 指出虽然有些人主张所有人都可以且应该使用迷幻药物，但实际上这种药物并不适合每个人。他们呼吁对迷幻药物的适用人群进行更深入的科学研究，并强调隐私和个人选择的重要性。

• [nashashmi] 认为伊斯兰教的教义明确禁止使用任何形式的致幻药物，并质疑那些声称通过迷幻药物获得宗教体验的可信度。他们强调，这种研究可能会将宗教信仰与幻觉混为一谈，这是一种逻辑谬误。

补充讨论：
• [quantified] 和 [xwowsersx] 对原文内容持批评态度，认为其缺乏深度和新意。
• [kelipso] 和 [testemailfordg2] 对迷幻药物的潜在风险表示担忧，前者以幽默的方式表达了自己的负面体验，后者则对提倡此类药物的文章持怀疑态度。
• [bravesoul2] 和 [Projectiboga] 提到历史上宗教领袖参与迷幻药物实验的案例，如Marsh Chapel实验，并对这种实验可能对世界的积极影响表示好奇。

争议焦点：
• 迷幻药物的精神性体验是否适用于所有人，以及如何识别不适合使用这些药物的人群。
• 迷幻药物体验与宗教体验的关系，是否可以将两者等同视之。
• 科学研究与宗教信仰之间的界限，以及如何避免将幻觉与宗教信仰混为一谈。

44293610.article_content:
Explore
A
lmost a decade ago, a Baptist Biblical scholar, a Catholic priest, several rabbis, an Islamic leader, a Zen Buddhist roshi, and more than a dozen other religious leaders walked into a lab—and took high doses of magic mushrooms.
Nautilus Members enjoy an ad-free experience.
Log in
or
Join now
.
All of them said it was their first time taking the drug. The
mind-altering details
of these guided trips were recorded at the time and over the following 16 months, but it wasn’t until recently that the results of the controversial experiment came to light.
One might wonder how a single psilocybin trip could compare to the catalog of rich transcendent experiences that might accumulate over a lifetime of religious devotion. But according to the
findings
, which were published in the peer-reviewed journal
Psychedelic Medicine
, the vast majority of the 33 clergy who participated in the study—more than 90 percent—said taking psilocybin was one of the most spiritually meaningful and deeply sacred experiences of their lives. Almost half said it was the most profound thing they had ever experienced, period. Many of them also said it made them better religious leaders.
Now, years later,
some of these clergy
have become evangelists for psychedelics, incorporating them into their own religious teachings. For some of them, the experience led to a release from attachment to dogmas and greater openness to other forms of religious experience. For at least one participant, it was a dark, empty, terrifying trip. Still, none of them ruled out using psilocybin again in the future.
Publication of the study took so long in part due to charges of ethical lapses, including potential conflicts of interest related to funding sources, as well as the direct involvement of a funder in the research itself. But these conflicts were eventually resolved through disclosure, which the authors say they always intended. Questions also swirled around certain flaws in the study’s execution, which even the authors, scientists at Johns Hopkins University and New York University, admit.
One issue was bias: Participants may have been primed to see their experiences as sacred by language used in recruitment ads and by the expectations of those running the experiment. (Many of those who chose to participate were also considering leaving the profession at the outset and so could have been seeking a way to reconnect with the divine.) The sample was also small, heavily white, male, and Christian; and representation of a number of major world religions, including Indigenous religious traditions, Hinduism, Taoism, and Confucianism, was absent.
ADVERTISEMENT
Nautilus Members enjoy an ad-free experience.
Log in
or
Join now
.
Still the results raise questions about the relationship between hallucinogens and religious experience. Most of the major world religions today (Hinduism, Judaism, Buddhism, Christianity, Islam) do not advocate the use of mind-altering substances. But psychedelic plants and mushrooms have been employed in sacred ceremonies by
Indigenous cultures
in the Americas for millennia, and many psychedelic researchers suspect they drove pagan mystical experiences in ancient Greece that may have served as the foundations for some religions, including
Christianity
.
William James, considered the father of American psychology and author of
The Varieties of Religious Experience
, is said to have to come to many of his own
most central ideas
at least in part through hallucinatory experiences with nitrous oxide: the value of religion, the importance of mystical experience, the universe as pluralistic. But transcendence is not an unequivocal good: As one religious scholar found, you can have
too much
of it.
Lead image: New Africa / Shutterstock
Kristen French
Posted on
June 12, 2025
Kristen French is an associate editor at
Nautilus
.

data.title: He's got the rights, the original code, and is about to relaunch Dungeon Rampage
data.author: danso
data.article_summary: Angelos Mako在七岁时开始与哥哥一起玩Facebook游戏《Dungeon Rampage》，这款游戏不仅带给他乐趣，还成为他父母离婚期间的情感寄托。然而，游戏在运营多年后突然关闭，年仅十岁的Mako决心将来要复活它。长大后，他通过Minecraft模组和Roblox积累了一些游戏开发经验，并在2024年接手了一个重制《Dungeon Rampage》的Discord项目。然而，项目进展缓慢，他决定直接联系原开发者以获取版权。经过一番努力，Mako成功获得了《Dungeon Rampage》的版权，但重制工作仍需从零开始。在寻求原开发者和行业专家的帮助后，Mako继续推动这个项目，努力实现复活经典游戏的梦想。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44301868.article_content:
Angelos Mako, now 18, started playing Dungeon Rampage over a decade ago.
(Image credit: Gamebreaking Studios)
Angelos Mako was seven years old when he started playing Dungeon Rampage with his older brother, saving the good guys and slaying hordes of evil minions. A decade later, he also saved the game itself.
Dungeon Rampage was a simple Facebook game, a cartoony hack-n-slash that was procedurally generated, so the dungeons were always a little different. But for Mako, it was also an escape.
"My parents were going through a very nasty divorce. Dungeon Rampage was there for me. Every time they would fight, I would go into another room and I would play," says Mako, now 18, from his home in Greece. "It took care of me when when no one else could."
Related articles
Publisher who resurrected lost pirate game Captain Blood says it's 'a 3 or 4' by today's standards, but that's half the fun: 'All its charms, all its flaws, all the vibes are from that era'
“That evening, I told the company: This is the first game we're publishing”—how vibes, fun, and aggressively mashing a keyboard landed the Vampire Survivors dev its first publishing client
The rights to one of the greatest PC games of all time languished in the vault of a Midwestern insurance firm until a frustrated player bugged them about a re-release, 'But they asked me if I wanted to do System Shock 3'
The end of the dungeon
Mako played DR daily, mostly on a computer he shared with his brother at home. It was a popular game in its time: More than two million people hopped in each month, and Mako was one of them for five years straight. Then the unthinkable happened.
"I came from school one day and saw a message Dungeon Rampage had shut down, and I was like, 'What?! Why?'" he says. "I couldn't fathom it. I couldn't understand why it happened. But even from that moment, I said that I'm going to find a way to get this back again. I had no clue how, but I had a dream."
Dungeon Rampage was played by millions back when Facebook games were thriving.
(Image credit: Gamebreaking Studios)
I was fed up. I wanted this to come to life. I said, 'Okay, I'm starting from scratch. I'm taking initiative.'
Angelos Mako
Still, Mako was only 10, had school to attend, and the dream had to wait. He got into mods in Minecraft, played some Roblox, and years later met a creator in a Roblox game. They bonded, and he did some apprenticeships on that team's game, in Unity. While he was doing that, four years later, he ran across a Discord server that was trying to remake Dungeon Rampage and decided to join.
"I really liked the vision," he says. But practical problems and volunteer developers meant the group didn't make a ton of progress, and they were trying to reinvent the game, rather than restore the original. Mako took over the project in 2024.

Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
"I didn't know that making a game is pretty hard," he says, laughing. At the same time, people were joining the server and asking a key question: What happened if the original developers chose to copyright strike the remake?
"We were like, 'Oh yes, that's a very big problem.' I was fed up. I wanted this to come to life," Mako says. "I said, 'Okay, I'm starting from scratch. I'm taking initiative.' And I went directly to try and get the copyright of Dungeon Rampage."
The sleuthing starts
Mako had the credits screen from the game, and decided that he'd make a LinkedIn account and message everyone he could find. "People replied, actually. That's the weird part."
He spoke with Jason Yeung, the original creative director, who said that the attempt to remake Dungeon Rampage was a cool project, but that he needed to speak with Mike Goslin, who had run Rebel Entertainment, the original Dungeon Rampage developer. One thing led to another: He spoke to Goslin on the phone, who then introduced him to the CEO of the parent company—and he got his license agreement.
Mako was ecstatic. Only one thing brought him back to earth: "Because I started from scratch again, we didn't really have a game," he says. So he talked with all the developers of the original game that he could find. The original lead artist got him some art source files. But no one seemed to have the code.

Mako messaged him to ask exactly what that was

data.title: Snorting the AGI with Claude Code
data.author: beigebrucewayne
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI生成内容、代码处理工具（如Claude Code）及其在软件开发中的应用和影响的讨论。

不同观点：
• **反对依赖AI生成摘要和内容**：mjrbrennan认为AI生成的总结往往内容冗长、写作风格差，且事实准确性存疑，不如直接阅读原始文本或查看提交记录来得快和可靠。
• **对AI工具能力的认可**：jumski和SamPatt认为Claude Code在处理多任务、复杂问题（如竞态条件和bug追踪）方面表现出色，尤其是在结合其他工具（如sigoden/aichat）时效果显著。此外，Claude Code被视为一种多功能的工具，而不仅仅是代码编辑器。
• **对AI工具使用的经济性和模型选择的关注**：Syzygies指出不同AI模型（如Opus 4）在性能和成本上的差异，强调选择合适的模型对工作效率和成本的影响。
• **对自动化工作流的实用性和局限性的讨论**：tinyhouse认为文章中提到的自动化工作流功能并非全新，且对AGI的提及没有必要；而dirtbag__dad则关注模型生成的代码对团队代码审查习惯和长期质量的影响。
• **对AI工具长期影响的担忧**：b0a04gl担心模型生成的描述、测试和代码可能会降低团队对风险的敏感性，进而影响代码质量。

补充讨论：
• **法律条款和信任问题**：bionhoward对Anthropic的法律条款表示担忧，认为其条款难以满足，可能会影响对其产品的信任。
• **工具界面的可读性和用户体验**：AstroBen提到评论的背景和文字对比度问题，影响了阅读体验。
• **对未来程序员职业的乐观态度**：tom_m认为无论AI如何发展，程序员的职业始终会有需求。
• **对AI生成内容成本和道德问题的讨论**：dweinus对AI生成内容的成本、环境影响及版权问题提出了质疑，反映了一些用户对AI工具使用背后更深层次的顾虑。

争议焦点：AI生成内容和工具的可靠性、实用性及长期影响。

data.title: Make little apps for you and your friends
data.author: 8organicbits
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了由John和Pontus开发的研究原型Scrappy，一个用于为亲友制作简易应用程序的工具。与市场上的大众软件或企业定制软件不同，Scrappy旨在让普通人为自己和所爱之人创建个性化、富有表达力的软件。文章通过几个例子展示了Scrappy应用的可能性，如算术练习工具、活动出席计数器、会议成本计时器和家务跟踪器。Scrappy提供一个无限的交互对象画布，用户可以通过类似Figma或Google Slides的界面，为对象添加行为和少量代码来构建应用。Scrappy应用支持多人协作、持久化状态和选择性分享，且编辑和运行无明显区分。该项目的目标是重新构想软件的创作和使用方式，推动"小型计算"和"家庭自制软件"运动，让普通用户无需成为专业程序员也能表达自我。

44306859.article_content:
Software is important to people. Most of us spend our workdays in front of computers. We use the computer in our pocket tens if not hundreds of times every day. The apps we use are almost exclusively mass-market, sold on an app-store, made for thousands if not millions of users. Or they are enterprise apps that are custom-built for hundreds of thousands of dollars.
But there isnât really any equivalent of home-made software â apps made lovingly by you for your friends and family. Apps that arenât polished or flashy, but are made to
your
preference
and help you with
your particular needs.
Weâre John and Pontus, and weâve been exploring the potential of home-made software together.
We ended up creating a research prototype that we call
Scrappy
â a tool for making
scrappy apps for just you and your friends.
First and foremost, we aim to contribute a
vision
of what home-made software could be like. We want to make this vision as concrete as we can, by sharing a working tool and examples of apps made in it. Scrappy, in its current state, is a prototype, not a robust tool, but we hope it paints the picture we carry in our heads â of software as something that can be creative, personal, expressive. Made by anyone, for themselves and their loved ones.
What is Scrappy?
It may not be clear what âa scrappy app for you and your friendsâ means. What kind of apps are these? Let us paint a picture with a few examples. (We call them â

Certain objects, like buttons, has attributes like âwhen clickedâ that contain javascript code. When the button is clicked, that code is run â maybe it records the contents of the textfield to a label that acts as a log. I start out by adding a number field to track the number of attendees, and two buttons for recording people entering and exiting the venue.

Without any extra work, Scrappy apps are multiplayer.

Thereâs no distinction between editing and running. I can edit the app while a friend is using it.

Outside the shared frame are a bunch of fields used to compute the cost of the meeting. This lets me see the data while Iâm working on the Scrapp, just like in a spreadsheet, which is very helpful for debugging â and it makes future tweaking or remixing easier.

44306859.article_summary: 文章介绍了由John和Pontus开发的研究原型Scrappy，一个用于为亲友制作简易应用程序的工具。与市场上的大众软件或企业定制软件不同，Scrappy旨在让普通人为自己和所爱之人创建个性化、富有表达力的软件。文章通过几个例子展示了Scrappy应用的可能性，如算术练习工具、活动出席计数器、会议成本计时器和家务跟踪器。Scrappy提供一个无限的交互对象画布，用户可以通过类似Figma或Google Slides的界面，为对象添加行为和少量代码来构建应用。Scrappy应用支持多人协作、持久化状态和选择性分享，且编辑和运行无明显区分。该项目的目标是重新构想软件的创作和使用方式，推动"小型计算"和"家庭自制软件"运动，让普通用户无需成为专业程序员也能表达自我。

data.title: OpenSERDES – Open Hardware Serializer/Deserializer (SerDes) in Verilog
data.author: peter_d_sherman
data.article_summary: OpenSERDES 是一个使用 Skywater Open PDK 130nm 技术的可数字合成的 SerDes（串行器/解串器）架构。SerDes 将并行数据转换为串行数据流，通过高速连接（如 LVDS）传输，并在接收端转换回并行数据。该项目使用 OpenLane 和 Cadence Virtuoso 工具，Verilog HDL 编码，Sky130 CMOS 技术映射。主要组件包括：基于 CMOS 反相器的 TX 驱动器、使用电阻反馈反相器和 CMOS 反相器的可合成 Rx、DFF（数据采样）和 NAND 逻辑构成的主从 DFF，以及用于时钟和数据恢复的过采样 CDR。相关文件和仿真结果已上传至相应文件夹。项目采用 GPL-3.0 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源芯片设计的难度与现状

不同观点：
• [jauntywundrkind的观点] 开源CPU本身虽然看似容易制作，但要让芯片实际运行起来，涉及到许多其他复杂部分，如USB主机控制器、声卡芯片、DRAM控制器和PCIe模块等。大多数芯片设计依赖于预先验证过的模块化设计，而非完全从零开始。虽然某个项目已有五年历史且更新较少，但仅仅开始尝试设计能够与外界交互的开源芯片，已经是一个巨大的进步。开源芯片的发展需要通过不断的构建、表征、调整和尝试才能取得进展。

• [peter_d_sherman的观点] 提供了一本相关的书籍《High-Speed Serial I/O Made Simple: A Designers’ Guide, with FPGA Applications》(2005)，暗示通过学习相关技术文献可以更好地理解和进行芯片设计。此观点更倾向于借助已有文献和知识来推动芯片设计的发展。

补充讨论：
• jauntywundrkind强调了开源芯片设计中的现实困难，特别是模块化设计和验证的普遍性，以及开源芯片项目需要长期的迭代和实验。
• peter_d_sherman则提供了一个具体的学习资源，可能暗示通过系统的学习可以更有效地应对这些挑战。

OpenSERDES
Serializer/Deserializer (
SerDes
) is the most important functional block used in high speed communication.
SerDes converts parallel data into a serial (one bit) stream of data that is transmitted over a high-speed connection, such as LVDS, to a receiver that converts the serial stream back to the original, parallel data.
A global CLOCK signal is present to sequence the serialization and deserialization of data from one block to another.
Technology:
Skywater OpenPDK 130nm
Tools Used:
OpenLane, Virtuoso Cadence
The
Serializer
and
Deserializer
blocks are coded in Verilog HDL and synthesized using Openlane tool mapped to Sky130 CMOS technology. Simulation results and associated gds, spice and netlist files are uploaded in Serializer and Deserializer folders respectively
A chain of CMOS inverters is used as TX driver to drive the input capacitance of the channel. The gds, spice, netlist and. oa files for the same are present in
Inverter_Based_Tx
folder
A fully synthesizable Rx is designed using Resistive FB inverter followed by CMOS inverter as sensing and gain element respectively. The following DFF is used to sample the data using the clock recovered by the CDR.
Resistive Feedback inverter
is used as sensing element to sense low amplitude received signal at the front end of the receiver. Details of the implementation of Resistive FB inverter can be found in Resistive_FB_inverter folder
DFF is the simplest memory block to sample and store the data before deserializing. Master Slave DFF is implemented using NAND logic gates. Details of the same are present in
DFF
and
NAND
folders
Oversampling CDR
is used to recover the data and clock from the received signal. The CDR uses the data transitions to tune the clock frequency for proper decoding of received signal. The
Oversampling_CDR
folder contains the gds, spice and synthesized Verilog files generated from Openlane tool.
